To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glycotype of PrPsc is different in different forms of CJD and that PrP27_30 glycotype analysis may be useful for differential diagnosis.

(i) the PrP27- 30 glycotype pattern is different in sporadic Creutzfelt-Jakob disease, familial Creutzfelt- Jakob disease and Gerstmann- Sträussler-Sheinker syndrome; (ii) the polymorphic residue at position 129 has a leading role on PrP27-3o mobility; (iii) the PrP mutant residues 102 and 200 have a minor influence on PrP27 30 glycosylation pattern
the PrPsc glycotypes of sCJD, Val210lle f CJD and GSS are type 1, while the PrPsc of Glu200L ys fCJD is type 1B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterisation of PrPsc in different forms of CJD and GSS, and provides new information on the relationship between PrPsc molecular structure and pathogenesis of TSEs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PrPsc glycotype is not only a diagnostic tool but is also a powerful marker of the molecular pathogenesis of TSEs.

(a) PrP27- 30 glycotypes are different in different TSEs; (b) PrP27 -30 glycotypes can be used to identify TSE forms and, in the future, may be useful to discriminate between TSE forms with similar clinical presentation; (c) PrP27_30 glycotypes may be used to identify the polymorphic codons of the PrPgene and to identify the presence of a PrP mutation.
the PrP27- 30 glycotypes are determined by a combination of the polymorphic residue in position 129 of PrPC and the residue in position 200 of PrPsc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polymorphic codons 129 and 219 are involved in the determination of PrP27- 30 glycotypes, whereas the codons 102, 200, 211 and 217 are involved in the PrP27-3O glycosylation ratios.
the PrP27- 30 glycotypes are useful for distinguishing different TSEs, and the PrP27 30 glycotype 1A is a good indicator for sporadic and familial CJD.
the polymorphic codons 129 and 210 are the most important determinants of the PrPsc molecular weight in CJD and GSS, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PrPsc glycotypes are not only markers of disease but also markers of the molecular mechanism of disease pathogenesis.
the PrP27- 30 glycosylation profile is a useful tool for distinguishing sCJD and fCJD.
the PrP27- 30 glycoprofile is a useful tool for the classification of CJD and other TSEs.
